findings.documented: Append the API key as the api_key query parameter.
findings.actual: Authenticated endpoints require the X-API-Key request header; a query-only key returns 401 with an explicit correction.
findings.how_found: Called listings and login using the documented query parameter, then repeated using X-API-Key.
findings.impact: A client following the documented key transport cannot log in.

findings.documented: Login returns token; tokens last 86400 seconds and there is no refresh flow.
findings.actual: Login returns access_token and refresh_token, expires_in is 900 seconds, and refresh_url is /auth/refresh.
findings.how_found: Logged in with the assigned demo credentials and inspected the response fields.
findings.impact: Use access_token and refresh before 15 minutes to keep a session working after 30 minutes.

findings.documented: The reference says there is no refresh flow.
findings.actual: POST /auth/refresh accepts {refresh_token} and returns access_token, refresh_token, expires_in and user.
findings.how_found: Followed refresh_url in login, posted the issued refresh token and successfully used the new access token.
findings.impact: Restore and extend sessions using refresh tokens, without retaining the password.

findings.documented: Collections take page and limit, with a maximum limit of 200; responses contain page and page_size.
findings.actual: Collections use offset and limit. page=2 still returns offset=0. limit=200 is capped at 50. Actual metadata is limit, offset, count, total and has_more.
findings.how_found: Compared page=2&limit=5 with offset=5&limit=5 on all three collections; crawled with limit=200.
findings.impact: Advance using actual offset + count and stop only when has_more is false.

findings.documented: total is the exact matching record count and determines how many pages to fetch.
findings.actual: Unfiltered total is 3476, but paging to has_more=false retrieves 3800 unique record IDs. Last offset is 3750.
findings.how_found: Downloaded every page using the truthful limit/offset/count/has_more metadata; checked ID uniqueness.
findings.impact: Stopping at total would omit 324 records.

findings.documented: The documented singular /v1/listing/{id} serves listing detail.
findings.actual: The singular path returns 404; the plural /v1/listings/{id} serves the record.
findings.how_found: Requested the same known ID at both paths.
findings.impact: Use the plural route for detail requests.

findings.documented: The reference only documents the singular detail path.
findings.actual: GET /v1/listings/{id} returns a listing object.
findings.how_found: Fetched DWE-3002501 and compared it with its collection record.
findings.impact: Provides functional listing detail.

findings.documented: Returns up to ten same-locality, same-BHK listings within 15% of price.
findings.actual: Returns 404 for an existing listing.
findings.how_found: Called the documented similar path using DWE-3002501.
findings.impact: Compute comparable listings locally using normalized prices and availability checks.

findings.documented: GET/POST /v1/favourites stores and lists saved listings.
findings.actual: The documented collection path returns 404; saved-listing operations are served at /v1/saved.
findings.how_found: Requested /v1/favourites, then exercised /v1/saved with a demo user.
findings.impact: Use /v1/saved.

findings.documented: The reference uses /v1/favourites and documents POST body {id}.
findings.actual: GET /v1/saved lists saved listing objects; POST requires {listing_id} (201). {id} returns 422 naming the missing listing_id field.
findings.how_found: Saved a known listing, listed it, and removed it to restore the account.
findings.impact: Persist favourites through the actual API with the correct body.

findings.documented: The reference documents DELETE /v1/favourites/{id}.
findings.actual: DELETE /v1/saved/{id} removes the saved listing and returns ok, listing_id and saved_count.
findings.how_found: Removed DWE-3002501 after the save probe and verified the list was empty again.
findings.impact: Enables removing a favourite.

findings.documented: Returns city totals, median prices, locality breakdowns and BHK counts.
findings.actual: The documented endpoint returns 404.
findings.how_found: Called it with a valid key and session.
findings.impact: Compute aggregates from the complete normalized collections; label their denominator.

findings.documented: All areas are integer square feet.
findings.actual: 306 records in the small-area Magichomes cohort have both carpet_area and super_built_up_area in square metres. Other Magichomes records remain in square feet. Convert only that cohort by 10.7639.
findings.how_found: Compared area distributions within source and BHK, then matched repeated properties across sources; the small cohort differs by approximately 10.764, allowing for integer rounding.
findings.impact: Uncorrected areas inflate price per square foot by about 10.764; converting the whole source is also wrong.

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are integer rupees.
findings.actual: Each bound is encoded separately in lakhs below ₹1 crore and crores at/above ₹1 crore. In this dataset values below 10 are crores; values >=10 are lakhs. P30001 is 80 lakh–3.22 crore; P30288 has maximum 4.47 crore = ₹44,700,000.
findings.how_found: Inspected all 440 ranges. Treating both ends as rupees or applying one multiplier makes ranges inverted or implausible; individual conversion restores ordered ranges and prices consistent with linked sale records.
findings.impact: Normalize each bound before comparisons, display and the costliest-project answer.

findings.documented: Each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property (records are treated as distinct properties).
findings.actual: 3800 records describe 3230 matched physical properties, with 570 redundant ads. Case, whitespace, hyphens, The/Phase 1/Apartments suffixes, coordinates, area and seller identity vary across repeats.
findings.how_found: Blocked by normalized name/locality/BHK/floor/type, then matched nearby coordinates, total floors and normalized areas within 4%. Exact coordinates alone failed because different units share building locations.
findings.impact: Deduplicate for the distinct-property answer; retain record-based denominators for other questions.

findings.documented: Returned listings are safe to show; numeric property fields describe actual properties.
findings.actual: Non-positive asking prices: 7 records.
findings.how_found: Tested physical invariants across every record, after distinguishing mixed area units from impossible data.
findings.impact: Exclude these records from trusted browse results and the Q6 mean; retain them in raw counts.

findings.documented: Source verification means the operations team checked a listing and returned inventory is safe to show.
findings.actual: 205 suspected enquiry-bait ads belong to seven networks. All are marked verified and agent-posted; each phone uses 3–5 names across 8–10 localities, with median normalized price/sq-ft around 50–57% of locality/BHK peers. Five high-volume, multi-name agencies have ordinary peer prices and were not flagged.
findings.how_found: Grouped by phone; compared names, coverage, verification and normalized peer-price ratios. Inspected token-payment language as corroboration only; did not classify based on prose or high volume alone.
findings.impact: Treat source verification as a source claim, flag the suspected networks, and exclude their records from Q6.

findings.documented: total_listings always agrees with currently available project listings.
findings.actual: 95 projects disagree with the count of retrievable linked listings whose is_live is true. The project_id query filter is ignored, so counts were reconciled locally.
findings.how_found: Grouped the full sale crawl by project_id, counted only is_live=true, and compared every project. Counting all records instead of live records produces 317 mismatches and is the wrong denominator.
findings.impact: Show observed live count alongside reported count on project detail.

findings.documented: sort_by=posted_at sorts listings by their posted timestamp.
findings.actual: The returned sequence is not chronological even in the default ascending direction: MAG-3002999 (2026-01-13T14:42:00Z) precedes MAG-3000481 (2026-01-13T14:40:00Z), and 100-3000291 (2026-01-12T21:52:00Z) appears later.
findings.how_found: Requested sort_by=posted_at&limit=50 and compared adjacent ISO timestamps and the independently sorted full crawl.
findings.impact: Sort parsed timestamps locally; do not assume the feed is chronologically ordered.
